scope: Bounded ownership/compatibility audit of the session-cache lifecycle in src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs: SSL_SESSION refcounts across SSL_CTX_add_session / SSL_CTX_remove_session / SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex / SSL_SESSION_free / SSL_set_session, the internal OpenSslStack cache, eviction, expiration, removal-callback re-entrancy, the automatic-flush trigger, and end-to-end TLS1.2 resumption under SSL_OP_NO_TICKET. Authority compared at source level against openssl-3.0.13 ssl/ssl_sess.c and ssl/ssl_lib.c.

flushing_decision.counter: sess_connect_good for SSL_SESS_CACHE_CLIENT, otherwise sess_accept_good; read before the caller's own post-handshake increment, exactly as the authority reads it inside ssl_update_cache
flushing_decision.error_behaviour: the flush returns void and has no error arm; a failed write lock makes it a no-op, as in the authority
flushing_decision.note: The authority's early 'session_id_length == 0' return precedes its auto-flush block and is preserved: an empty-id session does not flush.

defects.class: application callback invoked under a non-reentrant cache lock (reentrancy edge, AGENTS §21)
defects.description: SSL_CTX_add_session's eviction arm called ctx.remove_session_cb while holding ctx.lock. The crate's CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock reports recursive acquisition as failure (no deadlock), so a callback that re-entered SSL_CTX_add_session or SSL_CTX_remove_session silently failed: the re-entrant insert returned 0 and never mutated the cache. The authority has the same lock-held callback call (ssl_sess.c:784-790); this crate's previous code reproduced it.
defects.fix: Detach every entry first, unlock, then invoke the removal callback and release the detached cache reference outside the lock (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:740-761). The callback is invoked once per evicted entry with the same arguments and order as before; the callback is snapshotted so the loop never re-reads the context after a callback retires it.
defects.divergence: Deliberate safety correction: the callback observes an unlocked, consistent cache where the authority holds ctx->lock. Re-entry now succeeds instead of failing.
defects.witness: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_remove_callback_reentrant_insert_does_not_corrupt_the_cache (passes; the callback's insert returns 1 and a nested eviction is observed).

defects.class: non-failure-atomic insert: eviction ran before the push that could refuse
defects.description: The old order evicted size-cap entries and then pushed the new session. If OPENSSL_sk_new_null/OPENSSL_sk_push refused, the call returned 0 after having permanently removed live entries, so a refused insert did not leave the cache as it was. The replacement arm likewise released the incumbent before the push could be attempted.
defects.fix: Push first; only then replace the incumbent and evict down to session_cache_size (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:696-738). A refused push now returns 0 with the cache byte-for-byte unchanged, including an incumbent under the same key.
defects.witness: Code-level: the only remaining refusal points (up_ref, lock acquisition, container allocation, sk_push) all precede every cache mutation. The refusal path cannot be forced through the public API without an allocator-failure hook; NOT_RUN as a runtime injection.

defects.class: last-reference destructor (application ex_data free callbacks) executed under the cache lock
defects.description: Both the replaced incumbent's release and each evicted entry's release ran with ctx.lock held. When that release was the last reference, CRYPTO_free_ex_data ran the session's application ex_data destructors under the lock - a second reentrancy edge and a potential deadlock for an ex_data callback that touches the context.
defects.fix: All detached cache references are released after unlock (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:745-760). The displaced same-key incumbent is released without a removal callback, matching lh_SSL_SESSION_insert's substitution arm.
defects.witness: Covered by the same re-entrancy test plus the existing refcount_reentrancy_tests::session_free_reentrancy_is_defined_noop.

defects.class: compatibility: SSL_SESS_CACHE_UPDATE_TIME was applied only to new entries
defects.description: The authority updates c->time and recalcs the timeout unconditionally after the same-key decision (ssl_sess.c:798-801), so re-adding an already-cached session refreshes its expiry. The crate only did so when the key was absent, so an already-cached session could expire earlier than in the authority.
defects.fix: Apply the UPDATE_TIME update before the already-cached/new decision (src/ssl/ssl_sess.rs:673-682).
defects.witness: Code-level authority comparison; no court sets UPDATE_TIME. NOT_RUN as a differential.

defects.class: compatibility/behavioural: a negative flush cutoff expired every session
defects.description: SSL_CTX_flush_sessions(s, t: c_long) with a negative t cast t to u64 for sess_timedout, making it a huge cutoff and flushing the entire cache. The authority compares signed time_t values, so t < 0 expires nothing; only t == 0 flushes everything.
defects.witness: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_expiration_removes_the_session_and_lookup_misses asserts SSL_CTX_flush_sessions_ex(ctx, -1) leaves the cache intact and a positive cutoff removes it.

defects.class: recorded divergence closed: automatic cache flushing was not modelled
defects.description: ssl_update_cache documented that the authority's every-255-connections auto-flush was absent, so a long-lived context never expired sessions automatically.
defects.fix: Implemented the authority trigger and action (see flushing_decision).
defects.witness: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_auto_flush_fires_on_the_authority_counter_value (0xfe leaves the expired entry cached; 0xff flushes it while the current session survives).

defects_found_not_fixed.detail: lookup_sess_in_cache ignores SSL_SESS_CACHE_NO_INTERNAL_LOOKUP and the external get_session_cb arm (pre-existing Phase-17 reduction, documented in the function). Outside S30's bounded cache-lifecycle scope; retained and reported.

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_growth_past_limit_evicts_the_oldest_entry
tests.asserts: cache_size=2, adding a third session evicts the oldest (address), keeps exactly two entries, leaves owner NULL and one reference on the evicted session, increments sess_cache_full, and SSL_CTX_sess_number answers 2

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_expiration_removes_the_session_and_lookup_misses
tests.asserts: a negative cutoff expires nothing; a positive cutoff removes the timed-out session, runs the removal callback once with that address, clears owner; a later lookup misses and increments sess_miss

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_remove_callback_reentrant_insert_does_not_corrupt_the_cache
tests.asserts: the removal callback observes no held cache lock on every invocation, its re-entrant SSL_CTX_add_session returns 1, the nested eviction runs, and the final cache is exactly {newest, re-entrant insert} with per-session reference counts intact

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_remove_callback_reentrant_remove_does_not_corrupt_the_cache
tests.asserts: the removal callback re-enters with SSL_CTX_remove_session (returns 1) and then SSL_CTX_add_session (returns 1); both callbacks run unlocked, and the final cache is exactly {newest, re-entrant insert} with the removed and evicted sessions at one reference and owner NULL

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_inserted_looked_up_and_removed_session_is_released_exactly_once
tests.asserts: by address identity: the cache lookup answers the same block, refs go 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1, and the session's ex-data free callback records that exact address once

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_auto_flush_fires_on_the_authority_counter_value
tests.asserts: 0xfe does not flush; 0xff flushes the timed-out cached entry before the current session is counted, leaving the current session; ssl_update_cache does not increment the counter

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_tls12_resumption_without_tickets_reuses_the_session_id
tests.asserts: end-to-end memory-BIO TLS1.2 handshake with SSL_OP_NO_TICKET on both contexts: session id is 32 bytes, has_ticket == 0, the server cache holds the session, the second handshake reports SSL_session_reused == 1 on both peers (server resumed from its internal cache), and the resumed client session carries the identical session id

tests.name: cache_lifecycle_tests::ssl_sess_canary_detects_a_removal_callback_under_the_cache_lock

retained_divergences: Eviction and flushing walk the OpenSslStack in insertion order; the authority walks a calc_timeout-ordered list. Pre-existing and documented in the module header.
Removal callbacks run outside ctx->lock here and inside it in the authority (S30-D1). Deliberate safety correction.

Cache capacity: this crate keeps at most session_cache_size entries (push, then evict while num > size). The authority's lh_insert-then-'while num >= size' sequence leaves at most size-1 entries. The S30 test asserts this crate's capacity of N; the off-by-one is a recorded compatibility divergence, not a claimed parity.
ssl_update_cache declines to re-cache a session with not_resumable != 0; the authority's ssl_lib.c has no such test.
lookup_sess_in_cache ignores SSL_SESS_CACHE_NO_INTERNAL_LOOKUP and the external get_session_cb arm.
TLS1.2 NewSessionTicket remains a stateful cache lookup rather than the authority's stateless encrypted blob (module header).
